title: Enhancing charge stability of Ge quantum well heterostructures via SiGe layer composition engineering
authors: Ding-Ming Huang, Jun-Hang Liu, Han Gao, Jie-Yin Zhang, Jian-Huan Wang, Fang-Ze Liu, Xin-Yu Zhou, Yi Luo, Bin-Xiao Fu, Xiao-Fei Liu, Ji-Yin Wang, Jian-Jun Zhang, H. Q. Xu
abstract: Composition modulation is a powerful technique for designing materials with tailored properties, fueling the development of advanced semiconductor devices. In this work, we have implemented this technique into Ge quantum well heterostructures, offering a promising avenue to address the critical challenge of charge stability in spin qubit devices. Harnessing the atomic-scale precision of molecular beam epitaxy, we have engineered the band structure of the SiGe top barrier via graded composition modulation, thereby reducing charge accumulation states at the SiGe-dielectric interface and strengthening the effective confinement to the hole gases in the Ge quantum wells. The enhanced charge stability of composition-modulated SiGe/Ge quantum well heterostructures is confirmed in Hall devices, featuring an enlarged stable gate voltage range. We have further fabricated quantum dot devices from the composition-modulated SiGe/Ge quantum well heterostructures and observed remarkably low charge noise with an averaged amplitude of $0.46\,\mathrm{μeV}/\mathrm{\sqrt{Hz}}$ at $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$---the lowest reported value for Ge quantum wells grown on silicon. This exceptional charge stability of the quantum dots persists in the few-hole regime, with no observable voltage drift over $\sim$hours. With reduced charge noise and enhanced energy stability, composition-modulated SiGe/Ge heterostructures exhibit significant potential for applications in building high-performance quantum devices, including spin qubits with a long coherence time.
summary: This work engineers Ge quantum well heterostructures by modulating the SiGe barrier composition to solve the critical issue of charge instability in spin qubit platforms. By preventing charge accumulation at interfaces, the researchers achieved significantly enhanced gate voltage stability and measured ultra-low charge noise in quantum dot devices. This demonstrates a promising material pathway for building high-performance quantum computing hardware.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is enhancing the charge stability of Ge quantum well heterostructures, which is critical for building reliable spin qubit devices.
main_result: Composition modulation of the SiGe top barrier significantly enhances charge stability, leading to an enlarged stable gate voltage range and achieving remarkably low charge noise ($0.46\,\mathrm{\mu eV}/\mathrm{\sqrt{Hz}}$) in quantum dot devices.
method: The study combines molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) for material growth with advanced electrical characterization techniques, including Hall bar measurements for stability and current spectroscopy/Coulomb peak tracking for charge noise.
model_or_system: The physical system is a SiGe/Ge quantum well heterostructure. The key mechanism involves engineering the SiGe top barrier via graded composition modulation to prevent charge accumulation states at the SiGe-dielectric interface.
key_observables: Stable gate voltage range ($	ext{V}_{	ext{stable}}$), charge noise power spectral density ($	ext{S}_{\epsilon}$), and voltage drift over extended periods.
important_parameters: The low charge noise amplitude ($0.46\,\mathrm{\mu eV}/\mathrm{\sqrt{Hz}}$) and the ability to maintain stability over hours are key performance metrics.
main_assumptions: The effectiveness of the composition modulation technique in mitigating charge noise is assumed to translate into long coherence times for spin qubits.
figures_summary: Figures compare the electrical performance of constant vs. composition-modulated barriers, showing increased stable gate voltage range. Other figures detail material characterization (TEM, XRD) and quantitative measurements of charge noise using both current spectroscopy and Coulomb peak tracking.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of problem identification (charge instability), proposed solution (composition modulation), material validation (MBE/TEM), electrical characterization (Hall bar stability), and performance benchmarking (low charge noise in quantum dots).
why_interesting: The focus on charge noise and stability directly impacts the coherence time of qubits, making the material engineering and low-noise measurements highly relevant to open quantum systems research.
